scenes.tts: Why does a nerve terminal release more packets when there is more calcium?
scenes.visual: The nerve terminal, with a calcium icon and a question on screen.
scenes.narration: Why does a nerve terminal release more packets when there is more calcium?

scenes.tts: Start with the machinery. The action potential opens voltage-gated calcium channels in the terminal.
scenes.visual: A spike invades the terminal; calcium channels in the membrane open.
scenes.narration: Start with the machinery. The action potential opens voltage-gated calcium channels in the terminal.

scenes.tts: Calcium flows in, down a steep gradient.
scenes.visual: A cloud of calcium ions (Ca²⁺) forms just inside the open channels.
scenes.narration: Calcium flows in, down a steep gradient.

scenes.tts: Nearby vesicles are already docked and primed, ready to fuse.
scenes.visual: Vesicles sit against the membrane near the channels. Label: docked and primed.
scenes.narration: Nearby vesicles are already docked and primed, ready to fuse.

scenes.tts: Calcium binds a sensor protein, synaptotagmin.
scenes.visual: Calcium ions attach to a synaptotagmin on a vesicle. Label: synaptotagmin (calcium sensor).
scenes.narration: Calcium binds a sensor protein, synaptotagmin.

scenes.tts: That triggers the snare proteins to finish zipping. They pull the vesicle and the membrane into one.
scenes.caption: That triggers the SNARE proteins to finish zipping. They pull the vesicle and the membrane into one.
scenes.visual: A four-helix SNARE bundle (from the 1SFC structure) zips up, pulling the membranes together until they merge.
scenes.narration: That triggers the SNARE proteins to finish zipping. They pull the vesicle and the membrane into one.

scenes.tts: Release needs calcium outside the terminal. Magnesium opposes it.
scenes.visual: Two labels: calcium needed; magnesium opposes.
scenes.narration: Release needs calcium outside the terminal. Magnesium opposes it.

scenes.tts: Dodge and Rahamimoff measured how strongly, at the frog junction, in nineteen sixty-seven.
scenes.caption: Dodge and Rahamimoff measured how strongly, at the frog junction, in 1967.
scenes.visual: Names on screen: F. A. Dodge and Rami Rahamimoff, 1967.
scenes.narration: Dodge and Rahamimoff measured how strongly, at the frog junction, in 1967.

scenes.tts: They changed calcium step by step and plotted the response against calcium, both on log scales.
scenes.visual: Log-log axes draw: external calcium along the bottom, endplate potential amplitude up the side.
scenes.narration: They changed calcium step by step and plotted the response against calcium, both on log scales.

scenes.tts: At low calcium, the points fall on a steep straight line. Its slope is near four.
scenes.visual: Points appear one by one along a steep straight line. Label: slope near 4 (3.78 in their data).
scenes.narration: At low calcium, the points fall on a steep straight line. Its slope is near four.

scenes.tts: As calcium nears its normal level, the line bends over.
scenes.visual: Further points bend the line over toward the top right. Label: normal calcium.
scenes.narration: As calcium nears its normal level, the line bends over.

scenes.tts: A slope near four means release rises roughly as the fourth power of calcium.
scenes.visual: On screen: release ∝ [Ca]⁴, roughly, on the steep part.
scenes.narration: A slope near four means release rises roughly as the fourth power of calcium.

scenes.tts: On the steep part, double the calcium. How much more transmitter comes out?
scenes.visual: A doubling arrow along the calcium axis on the steep part. The question on screen.
scenes.narration: On the steep part, double the calcium. How much more transmitter comes out?

scenes.tts: Far more than double. With their measured slope, about fourteen times more.
scenes.visual: On screen: 2^4 = 16; with slope 3.78, 2^3.78 ≈ 14 times more.
scenes.narration: Far more than double. With their measured slope, about fourteen times more.

scenes.tts: That is why a modest loss of calcium entry can cut release sharply.
scenes.visual: The doubling arrow reverses; release drops steeply.
scenes.narration: That is why a modest loss of calcium entry can cut release sharply.

scenes.tts: Why so steep, and why does it bend? Picture four seats that must all be filled.
scenes.visual: A cartoon of four empty seats at one release site.
scenes.narration: Why so steep, and why does it bend? Picture four seats that must all be filled.

scenes.tts: In this picture, release at a site needs all four seats holding calcium at once.
scenes.visual: Only when all four seats hold a calcium ion does the vesicle fuse. Label: a picture, not a measured count of sites.
scenes.narration: In this picture, release at a site needs all four seats holding calcium at once.

scenes.tts: At low calcium, each seat is rarely filled. All four at once is rarer still.
scenes.visual: Low calcium: seats flicker and fill one at a time, rarely all together.
scenes.narration: At low calcium, each seat is rarely filled. All four at once is rarer still.

scenes.tts: So release grows very steeply as calcium rises. On log scales, that is a straight line of slope four.
scenes.visual: Back on the plot, the steep straight part highlights. Label: slope 4.
scenes.narration: So release grows very steeply as calcium rises. On log scales, that is a straight line of slope four.

scenes.tts: As calcium rises further, the seats fill up. Adding more calcium cannot help much, so the line bends over.
scenes.visual: High calcium: the seats stay full; the plot's bend highlights.
scenes.narration: As calcium rises further, the seats fill up. Adding more calcium cannot help much, so the line bends over.

scenes.tts: A model like this fits the slope. Adding magnesium lowered the response without changing the slope.
scenes.visual: A second parallel line, lower down on the straight part, labelled more magnesium: same slope.
scenes.narration: A model like this fits the slope. Adding magnesium lowered the response without changing the slope.

scenes.tts: That fits magnesium competing with calcium for the same seats.
scenes.visual: Magnesium ions take some of the seats in the cartoon; the lower parallel line stays on the plot.
scenes.narration: That fits magnesium competing with calcium for the same seats.

scenes.tts: But the slope does not count binding sites. Saturation and calcium spread in the terminal can shape it.
scenes.visual: Label on the plot: the slope describes a curve; it is not a count of sites. Two tags: saturation; calcium spread.
scenes.narration: But the slope does not count binding sites. Saturation and calcium spread in the terminal can shape it.

scenes.tts: Treat four calcium ions as a reading of one curve, not a molecular fact.
scenes.visual: Card: four calcium ions = a reading of one curve in one preparation.
scenes.narration: Treat four calcium ions as a reading of one curve, not a molecular fact.

scenes.tts: So calcium is a steep dial on the count. Lose some calcium entry, and you lose many packets.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: calcium is a steep dial on the count, m.
scenes.narration: So calcium is a steep dial on the count. Lose some calcium entry, and you lose many packets.
